descriptionChirho: The outermost or farthest point of a spatial extent, used for cosmic or geographic extremities. In Matt 24:31 and Mark 13:27, angels gather the elect 'from the ends (akron) of the heavens to the ends of them,' describing the uttermost limits of the sky. Arabic uses aqsa (أَقصى, 'farthest'), French extremite, Korean kkeut (끝, 'end'), Hindi chhoron (छोरों, 'ends/edges'), Spanish extremos. Hebrew equivalent is qtseh (קְצֵה, 'edge/end'). All four occurrences in these two clusters share the same cosmic-spatial 'extremity' sense.

labelChirho: tip, point (of a body part or object)
descriptionChirho: The very tip or point of a physical object or body part. In Luke 16:24, the rich man asks Lazarus to dip the tip (akron) of his finger in water; English glosses 'tip,' Arabic tarafa (طَرَفَ, 'tip/end'), Hindi nok (नोक, 'point/tip'), Spanish punta ('point/tip'). In Heb 11:21, Jacob worships leaning on the top (akron) of his staff; English glosses 'top,' Arabic ra's (رَأْس, 'head/top'), German Spitze ('point/tip'), Hindi sire (सिरे, 'end/tip'), Korean kkeut (끝). Both refer to the precise physical extremity of a small object (finger, staff) rather than cosmic/geographic extremity.
